acceptance.assertion: Before preparation and immediately before apply, authenticate current GitHub protected main as this authority's one-file merge descendant, prove required validate (3.10), validate (3.12) and registry-registration-preflight/freshness checks green for exactly that revision, and bind current source diff digest.

Before prepare-intent and immediately before apply, in addition to exact protected-main CI, deployed-source/Registry/manifest ancestry and reserved-executor predicates, collect two FRESH independent user-systemd HOST-namespaced manual observations; the first is appended to approval-intent before prepare, the second to source-precondition before apply. Verify Linger=yes via loginctl show-user alex -p Linger, and verify with findmnt/statvfs that the configured persistent user_unit_dir (/home/alex/.config/systemd/user), its timers.target.wants, and trusted drop-in directories are actual non-tmpfs durable RW Btrfs paths outside /run. After prepare, require intent.user_unit_dir to equal /home/alex/.config/systemd/user byte-for-path; otherwise refuse apply. The source and installed runtime must agree on the ENTIRE set of managed scheduler units: exactly both .service and .timer for bureau-halfhour-operator, bureau-curator, bureau-operator-control, bureau-verifier-control, bureau-closure-planner, and bureau-task-supply. If target adds or removes a managed name, FAIL CLOSED before any effect; this authority does not approve set migration. Snapshot for every managed path its present/absent state, SHA-256, mode, FragmentPath, UnitFileState, ActiveState/SubState and service Result/ExecMainStatus. Snapshot the persistent timers.target.wants enablement paths and link targets, including proof they are not masks or runtime-only overlays. At BOTH pre-effect checkpoints require ALL SIX managed timers enabled/active/waiting with persistent wants links, exact trusted intended OnCalendar schedules, finite future NextElapseUSecRealtime, LastTriggerUSec, AccuracyUSec and RandomizedDelayUSec. Prove for EVERY timer that immutable installed and target OnCalendar strings are equal, follow the continuously recurring all-days systemd calendar grammar `*-*-* *:...` (no business-hour/day-of-week/month restrictions), and match their OWN exact entries in metadata.runtime_host_persistence_preflight.approved_timer_schedules (no cross-unit substitution); verify actual systemd-analyze calendar recurrence samples, including transitions, and require maximum consecutive UTC elapse gap <= 2 hours and accuracy+randomized delay <= 15 minutes. A sparse/unprovable or changed schedule REFUSES the one-shot effect before prepare/apply. The effect-completion timestamp does not exist at a pre-effect checkpoint: do NOT pretend a future effect-completion-relative 3h deadline is proven there. At post-effect and post-restore readback, calculate deadlines from the actual newly observed finite next scheduled elapse plus bounded grace, never from a guessed future effect completion. Do not enable a disabled optional timer. If any unit is transiently running, defer the checkpoint until its last invocation has completed and the timer is waiting; reject disabled, inactive or unschedulable timers BEFORE prepare/apply, not after the one-shot effect. At BOTH independent host pre-effect checkpoints, for EACH of the six managed .service units record Result, ExecMainStatus, InvocationID, ExecMainStartTimestamp and ExecMainExitTimestamp plus current ExecStart/FragmentPath SHA and bound old release. Accept only Result=success, ExecMainStatus=0, a nonempty InvocationID, valid nonzero start and exit timestamps with exit >= start, and a completed invocation under the verified PRE source/launcher (not systemd default status values from a never-run unit). A finished one-shot unit may be inactive/dead; a still activating/running, unknown, never-run or unsuccessful unit FAILS CLOSED before the one-shot effect. Preserve each of the six enabled/active timer intents, OnCalendar schedules and persistent wants links; this particular authority admits no disabled timer and does not change any timer's enablement. For ALL twelve units, query DropInPaths before both checkpoints, including empty sets. Require exact pre-approved persistent drop-in paths and content SHA-256 and reject any runtime-only (/run/user), unexpected, masked or mutable drop-in. On this host the expected nonempty set is exactly bureau-verifier-control.service.d/20-grabowski-sqlite-wal.conf at /home/alex/.config/systemd/user/bureau-verifier-control.service.d/20-grabowski-sqlite-wal.conf with SHA-256 e4caecbcc882c9fb62b5bb696d4dee784cae6fa923b0569f3b5908b1274f9934; every other managed unit must have EMPTY DropInPaths. At BOTH pre-effect checkpoints, additionally collect a reproducible OLD-SOURCE queue-policy BASELINE from the authoritative StateStore: ready and claimable counts, the current immutable task/revision IDs of at least one named ready task, and its actual typed claim-admission decision/rejection (including worker capabilities, acceptance, PR/path scope and policy inputs). At both pre-effect checkpoints, comparator task ID, immutable revision and explicit worker-capability/policy inputs MUST be identical. If any comparator ID, revision or policy input changes between the two checkpoints, ABORT that prepared attempt without apply, retain the original approval-intent/source-precondition evidence and never amend the already-prepared intent. No re-baselining inside that intent is permitted. Any later legitimate attempt must begin a NEW separately authorized prepare-intent with its OWN first approval-intent baseline before prepare and its OWN second matching source-precondition baseline before apply; if such lifecycle renewal is not supported, retain an incident rather than bypass the mismatch. No pre-effect proceed-on-unavailable comparator is authorized. Service last-successful InvocationID and start/exit timestamps MAY advance through normal scheduled executions between checkpoints; ready/claimable counts MAY change. Record and validate those dynamic values separately at both observations, never demand byte equality across snapshots. Persist all host AND baseline observations in the EXISTING approval-intent and source-precondition evidence classes, explicitly validate immediately before each action, and stop before a single-use effect if any mandatory host predicate is unproven. Missing or changed PRE-effect task/revision/policy comparator is a hard fail-closed prerequisite for the one-shot effect, not a downgrade. A later changed post-effect task revision prevents claiming source-independent queue causation and requires a retained incident. No unsupported evidence class, invented automatic validator or reboot test is claimed.

Use the installed Grabowski systemd-user reserved bureau-runtime-refresh-apply executor with the exact immutable StateStore authority revision, caller ownership and currently held leases. Admit at most one effect; after uncertain outcomes reconcile against attempt/result/manifest/StateStore without blind retry.

After the reserved one-shot effect and BEFORE any single-use finalization or lease release, independently verify one protected main commit across immutable installed release, package tree, canonical Registry, manifest, launcher, and ALL twelve user-systemd fragments under exactly the intent-bound PERSISTENT /home/alex/.config/systemd/user, with per-file content SHA and mode. The entire managed set must still be exactly the six names established before effect, with no added/removed units, file masks, tmpfs fragments or /run/user-only substitutes. Readback includes durable Btrfs findmnt/statvfs, persistent timers.target.wants symlink targets and Linger=yes. For each managed unit, DropInPaths POST set MUST equal EXACTLY the unit's recorded PRE set, including each absolute path and SHA256. Empty POST is permitted only when that unit's PRE set was empty. Specifically bureau-verifier-control.service MUST retain /home/alex/.config/systemd/user/bureau-verifier-control.service.d/20-grabowski-sqlite-wal.conf with SHA256 e4caecbcc882c9fb62b5bb696d4dee784cae6fa923b0569f3b5908b1274f9934; any lost or new drop-in fails readback. Every timer must retain its recorded PRE UnitFileState and ActiveState/SubState; bureau-task-supply.timer must still be enabled/active/waiting and its persistent wants link valid. For ALL SIX services, do not accept a carried-over pre-effect Result=success/ExecMainStatus=0: record POST InvocationID, ExecMainStartTimestamp and ExecMainExitTimestamp and prove a DIFFERENT completed invocation with start STRICTLY AFTER the authoritative UTC effect-completion timestamp recorded in the validated one-shot result, exit >= start and Result=success/ExecMainStatus=0. Compare normalized UTC epoch-microseconds for trusted systemd service start/exit and UTC result completion using the same clock domain, and check boot identity or monotonic timestamps where available; never lexically compare locale-formatted timestamps or infer an ambiguous timezone, while exact POST fragment SHA, ExecStart, launcher/release target and Registry source are immutable and equal to protected main. The source/launcher binding must be observed at that post-effect invocation, not inferred from an old status. For all SIX timers require post-effect enabled/active with trusted finite future NextElapseUSecRealtime, current LastTriggerUSec and exact original OnCalendar schedule. Set a deadline per service from first scheduled post-effect next-elapse plus min(max(2 times its verified interval, 15 minutes), 2 hours), with NO absolute cap relative to effect completion that could precede the first future real elapse. The deadline is calculated from the current user-manager's actual first post-effect next elapse (UTC microseconds) plus bounded grace, validated against the unchanged continuous all-days calendar; never use a guessed pre-effect next elapse. A missing new invocation BEFORE its deadline is PENDING_POST_EFFECT_INVOCATION with leases retained; no second one-shot effect and no false CASE C. An invalid/infinite next elapse, a failed fresh invocation, or absence of verified source-bound success AFTER its finite deadline is RUNTIME_CONVERGENCE_FAILED, requiring CASE C incident/rollback. No optional timer may be silently enabled or triggered; all six had to pass the pre-effect enabled/waiting predicate. Classify independent post-effect evidence as two separate predicates. RUNTIME_CONVERGENCE_OK requires exact protected source/Registry/manifest/launcher and persistent unit/drop-in/timer readback, six successful service results, a functioning Bureau doctor core runtime and an actual successfully completed task-supply/scheduler execution on that same source; a fallback scout or a bare success receipt is not enough. NORMAL_TASK_THROUGHPUT_OK separately requires an ordinary ready task to be claimed, executed and closed through current worker capability/acceptance/PR-binding rules. If runtime convergence is proven but throughput is blocked, classify INDEPENDENT_QUEUE_POLICY_BLOCKER ONLY when a stable, same-revision named ready task has the same typed rejection before and after the effect under unchanged policy inputs; match the prior approval-intent and source-precondition baselines, exact task/worker capabilities and deployed routing-code diff. A novel rejection, changed task revision or absent comparator is NOT independently proved: classify as possible source regression (CASE C if evidenced) or AMBIGUOUS_UNPROVEN (incident and leases retained), not automatic benign policy. Record current ready/claim counts, exact comparator and reject proof inside immutable-readback. When independence is proven, do not claim NORMAL_TASK_THROUGHPUT_OK or roll back correctly converged release; record throughput_status=INDEPENDENT_QUEUE_POLICY_BLOCKER and successor_issue=heimgewebe/bureau#2362, verify that issue is still OPEN, and finalize ONLY this narrower runtime authority. The overall P0 normal task throughput remains uncompleted until #2362 has a genuine ordinary claim-execute-close receipt. Any source, persistent runtime, doctor core or task-supply failure is RUNTIME_CONVERGENCE_FAILED and enters CASE C. If causal classification is ambiguous, preserve the incident and leases without claiming success or blindly retrying. Existing allowed immutable-readback and state-store-integrity evidence must include both manual host observations, post-effect snapshot, release/Registry diff, and incident/rollback result if any. A successful effect result is NOT proof of independent readback, normal claimability, reboot survival or successful closeout.

After complete immutable runtime readback, including all six NEW source-bound invocations and either NORMAL_TASK_THROUGHPUT_OK or an independently classified unchanged queue blocker with the verified OPEN successor issue heimgewebe/bureau#2362 recorded as throughput_status and successor_issue in the existing immutable-readback evidence, finalize ONLY this single-use source/runtime-convergence authority and release its exact Grabowski resource leases. Ordinary Bureau task routing, claim, execution and closure are still a separate P0 and shall be accepted only through their own reviewed contracts and real claim-execute-close receipts. This authority grants no NixOS/Pop!_OS disk mutation, repo writer of another lane, general queue or claim mutation, GitHub merge or product deployment.

rollback.strategy: Maintain an intact integrity-verified pre-effect Bureau source release 4dbd918736489a9faa892bafc8c7bb77c3f0c5c7, manifest, Registry snapshot, launchers and entire INTENT-BOUND per-path scheduler preimage before any apply. The complete snapshot includes twelve managed service/timer fragment files and every persistent wants-link and active-state intent, each exact present/absent state, per-path SHA/mode, and ALL approved persistent DropInPaths including the verifier WAL override hash; it also records absence for any candidate-introduced path and the pre-effect Linger+mount facts. Never hard-code a count of six files. CASE A: For in-process apply failure, the installed converge_user_scheduler exception path and rollback_effect can restore its native tracked scheduler fragments, enablement links and release pointers. Those helpers do NOT by themselves establish restoration of arbitrary service drop-ins or every service runtime property. Reobserve every recorded preimage item; any uncovered mutation/drop-in/drift requires separately authorized incident recovery and blocks authority finalization. CASE B: For process crash, host reboot or started.json with no authoritative validated result, resume_policy=never. Do not repeat the one-shot executor, auto-consume authority, infer success from absent output, or discard rollback artifacts. Reconcile actual manifest, Registry, launchers, fragment and DropInPath inventories first, then restore exact previous preimage through a SEPARATELY authorized recovery route if any mismatch is observed. The exhausted TaskSpec never grants itself incident-recovery powers. CASE C: If apply reports deployed/already_current but the independent source, persistency, DropInPaths, service health, Linger, doctor core runtime or task-supply readback fails (RUNTIME_CONVERGENCE_FAILED), treat the FULLY or partly switched release alike as an UNPROVEN failed outcome: do NOT finalize the authority or release leases as success. A real post-effect invocation failure or other evidenced runtime/source/doctor/timer failure is CASE C. Missing NEW post-effect InvocationID/timestamps BEFORE each timer-specific finite deadline is PENDING_POST_EFFECT_INVOCATION, not proof of success or failure: preserve leases without second effect. Missing or failed source-bound invocation AFTER that deadline (or invalid/infinite next elapse) is RUNTIME_CONVERGENCE_FAILED and enters CASE C. A separately proven unchanged same-task rejection against BOTH pre-effect queue baselines with healthy source+doctor core+task-supply (INDEPENDENT_QUEUE_POLICY_BLOCKER) is NOT CASE C; record throughput_status and the still-open successor heimgewebe/bureau#2362 in immutable-readback and close only the narrowed runtime/Registry task. If the rejection is NEW, code-attributable, source drifted, or the causal partition is uncertain, classify source regression or AMBIGUOUS_UNPROVEN, retain incident and leases and do not assert a successful closeout or execute unsupported recovery. Retain the exact successful result and started/intent receipts; invoke separately authorized out-of-band incident recovery to re-activate the retained previous release/manifest/Registry/launchers and all original unit+drop-in files and links, delete only exact target-introduced paths whose preimage provably recorded absence within the approved scope, then reobserve. ALL cases share the SAME required ROLLBACK READBACK before recovery closure: old source 4dbd918736489a9faa892bafc8c7bb77c3f0c5c7 package and Registry/manifest/launcher SHA, ALL per-path fragment modes/hashes, exact pre-effect DropInPaths sets and SHA, persistent wants-link targets, every timer UnitFileState and ActiveState/SubState, six completed post-RESTORE invocations bound to the restored old launcher, registered source, fragment and Registry, each with NEW InvocationID, ExecMainStartTimestamp after authoritative rollback completion, valid ExecMainExitTimestamp, Result=success and ExecMainStatus=0 (old cached success values do NOT count), Linger=yes, durable Btrfs mount and Bureau doctor. After rollback, for each of the SIX originally enabled timers, require finite trusted next UTC elapse and a NEW completed old-source-bound invocation within the same deadline formula: first scheduled elapse plus min(max(2 times the verified original interval, 15 minutes), 2 hours), with no arbitrary restore-completion-relative cap that could precede the actual next scheduled restored-source elapse; calculate the deadline from real post-restore NextElapseUSecRealtime and bounded grace. Before that deadline retain the recovery incident and leases; missing or failed proof after deadline is failed recovery requiring separately authorized remediation, never a claimed completed rollback. Do not automatically start or enable timers. If recovery is unavailable or any check fails, preserve blocked incident, old artifacts, logs and leases under applicable policy without asserting success. This authority NEVER changes NixOS, Pop!_OS, other repositories, any foreign task/lease, or bypasses Captain.
